stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model trending on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and performance tracking for a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-5.6 after government greenlight — and announces ‘ChatGPT Work’
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI has publicly rolled out GPT-5.6 following regulatory approval from the Trump administration.
The release coincides with the announcement of a new enterprise offering, 'ChatGPT Work'.
The model was previously available only in a limited preview for government-approved organizations.

stories.title: OpenAI may have made a fatal misstep in copyright fight with news orgs
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: OpenAI faces potential sanctions regarding its handling of data in copyright litigation.
The core issue involves allegations that OpenAI deleted or concealed ChatGPT usage logs during a copyright dispute with news organizations.
This incident highlights growing legal and ethical scrutiny over how large language models handle user data and intellectual property.

stories.title: GPT-5.6
stories.author: logickkk1
bullet_points: The news pertains to a potential new or updated OpenAI model, referenced as GPT-5.6.
The content links to official OpenAI deployment safety documentation and API guides, suggesting a formal release or update.
The topic is highly relevant as it concerns the latest advancements in large language models (LLMs) from a leading AI developer.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a language model.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting it is a contemporary LLM release.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when Gemma 4 is utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution into the personal AI agent ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Macs.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for local, high-speed AI inference on Apple devices.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Google will now tell you if an ad was made with AI
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Google is implementing a new feature to disclose if ads on its platforms (Search, Discover, YouTube) were created or edited using AI.
The disclosure will appear in a new 'My Ad Center' section under the 'how this ad was made' tab.
This move signals a growing industry trend toward transparency regarding the use of generative AI in advertising content.

stories.title: Microsoft’s patch Tuesdays are about to get bigger
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding the scope of its Patch Tuesdays for Windows 11.
The company is integrating AI into its update process to identify security vulnerabilities earlier.
This AI-driven approach will result in a higher volume of security fixes being delivered in each release.

stories.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a new tool, rebranded as Codex, aimed at automating and assisting user workflows.
The new tool promises independent operational capabilities, suggesting longer, autonomous task execution.
This signals a move toward more integrated and persistent AI agents capable of handling complex, multi-step tasks.

stories.title: Humanoid robots controlled by surgeons did world-first operation on live pigs
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Humanoid robots are being tested for use in surgical procedures.
The trial involved a world-first operation performed on live pigs.
The research aims to assess the feasibility of integrating robotics into complex surgeries.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current Vision-Language Model (VLM) evaluation: reliably assessing reasoning capabilities for safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advances in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving understanding beyond general scene recognition.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Traditional LLM evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient for assessing post-training quantization effects.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to measure behavioral changes post-quantization.
This research addresses a critical gap in deploying LLMs efficiently in resource-constrained environments.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training is effective, showing that training these critical parameters in isolation harms accuracy.
Demonstrates that the concept of Super Weights and their impact is not universally applicable across all Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents.
Addresses limitations of existing benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluation.
Aims to provide a more rigorous evaluation framework for real-world, complex tasks involving LLMs and multimodal agents.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
Traditional single-agent ReAct systems struggle with complex tasks due to limited context and single-trajectory constraints.
The research addresses the gap in existing multi-agent systems by improving recursive depth and search coverage beyond simple parallel execution.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits.
It proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
UltraX aims to overcome limitations in existing refinement methods, such as the rigidity of rule-based approaches.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality is now available, enhancing the model's access to real-time information.

stories.title: Microsoft’s carbon emissions went up 25 percent last year
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft's carbon emissions rose by 25% in 2025, according to its 2026 sustainability report.
The increase occurred despite the company's stated climate goals, suggesting challenges in meeting them.
The primary driver for the emission increase was attributed to the expansion of Microsoft's operations.

stories.title: Fidji Simo steps down from leading OpenAI’s AGI work due to illness
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI's AGI chief, Fidji Simo, is stepping down from her full-time role.
The departure is attributed to her ongoing health issues, specifically a neuroimmune condition.
Simo will transition to a part-time advisory role following her resignation.

stories.title: Netflix reportedly considers adding always-on channels
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly exploring the addition of always-on streaming channels.
This feature would allow users to stream specific shows and movies continuously.
The move positions Netflix to compete with ad-supported, always-on services like Pluto TV and Tubi.

stories.title: The ChatGPT browser is already dead
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI is sunsetting ChatGPT Atlas, its experimental browser feature.
Atlas, which allowed ChatGPT to perform tasks on the user's behalf, was launched less than a year ago.
The shutdown was announced as part of a broader update regarding ChatGPT Work features.

stories.title: Patch for Windows Defender 0-day could allow attackers to fill hard disk
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A vulnerability (0-day) in Windows Defender has been identified.
Exploitation of this flaw could potentially allow attackers to fill a hard disk.
The ongoing conflict between NightmareEclipse and Microsoft is noted as unresolved.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a new approach to enabling reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a temporal alternative to traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning.
Addresses the current limitation of existing video generators lacking diverse supervision specifically for CoF reasoning.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI systems' ability to understand scientific idea inheritance.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having a 'genome'—inheriting, repairing, and recombining prior work.
Focuses on two key capabilities: scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
Data was collected from a substantial sample of 77,543 distance learning students, offering robust behavioral insights.
It addresses a gap in current research by moving beyond small samples and self-reported survey data to analyze actual usage patterns.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent, Lisp-inspired conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows.
Focuses on 'Semantic Persistence' to better handle complex workflow elements like tool use, branching, and checkpointing.
Uses abstract concepts (symbolic forms, object identity) as explanatory lenses rather than rigid implementation requirements.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The study tests LLMs' ability to act as data annotators, showing AMALIA achieves high agreement with human coders.
The research cautions that high agreement (reliability) does not guarantee validity when inferring complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has relevance across fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The research challenges the assumption that low forward-marginal error in score matching guarantees numerical stability during diffusion sampling.
The study demonstrates that a smooth score field with small forward error can still lead to a nonexplosive and stable reverse-time process.
This highlights a critical distinction between theoretical error bounds (forward marginals) and practical stability during the sampling trajectory (reverse-time sampler).

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this latent graph enhances data sensemaking capabilities.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The research introduces ARDY, a new model for generating realistic 3D human motions.
It addresses the trade-off between offline methods (high control, slow inference) and online methods (fast inference, low control).
ARDY aims to provide real-time synthesis while maintaining controllability and handling complex semantic inputs for interactive applications.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
The authors propose 'BioModule,' a lightweight temporal transformer designed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The application scope is broad, covering fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of translating language model reasoning capabilities to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing autoregressive variational inference.
Aims to provide the necessary granularity for spatial understanding and precise motor control in AI agents.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses the limitations of current methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where crucial information gets lost in growing trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over long time spans.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in reinforcement learning.
It focuses specifically on citation quality verification within deep-research systems, where claims must be source-grounded.
The research investigates the calibration and potential bias of LLMs when evaluating structured citation attribution rubrics.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
The Domino drafter incorporates a GRU-based causal correction, allowing for path-dependent token distributions.
This new structure addresses a limitation in existing tree methods like DDTree, which rely on factorized marginals.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations (2,053 instances) to address limitations in current LLM evaluation.
Identifies significant variability in communication patterns and emotional expression among actual users.
Proposes a novel patient simulator designed to model clinical content, emotional state, and conversational strategy.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory despite sparse activation.
Identifies a limitation in existing pruning methods: they are designed for dense transformers and ignore the interdependent nature of MoE routing.
Introduces MAESTRO, a new method designed to intelligently prune 'bad experts' in MoE models using Markov-chain approaches.

stories.title: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
stories.author: SweetSoftPillow
bullet_points: A PostgreSQL implementation has been successfully rewritten using the Rust programming language.
The new Rust-based Postgres version has passed all existing Postgres regression tests.
This represents a significant effort in modernizing core database infrastructure using Rust's safety features.

stories.title: Browser Fingerprinting – How websites track you across internet –without cookies
stories.author: hackstar
bullet_points: Browser fingerprinting is a tracking method used by websites.
It allows tracking of users across the internet without relying on traditional cookies.
This represents a significant privacy concern in web browsing.

stories.title: Cpp2Rust: Automatic Translation of C++ to Safe Rust
stories.author: github.com via gnyeki
bullet_points: Cpp2Rust proposes an automatic translation tool to convert C++ code into Rust.
The focus is on achieving 'safe Rust' from potentially unsafe C++ codebases.
This addresses the growing need for interoperability and modernization between C++ and Rust ecosystems.

stories.title: Return on Attention: Why AI Code Reviews Are Wearing Us Out
stories.author: cseeman
bullet_points: AI code reviews are leading to increased PR volume without corresponding improvements in ticket quality.
The review process is increasingly automated, involving LLMs reviewing and responding to each other.
The core issue identified is broader than just code review, suggesting systemic problems in development workflows.

stories.title: I Built a Linter That Catches the Security Bugs AI Assistants Keep Writing
stories.author: ri5hu
bullet_points: The article discusses the growing reliance on AI coding assistants (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude).
The author developed a custom linter specifically designed to identify security vulnerabilities introduced by AI-generated code.
This highlights a critical emerging challenge: ensuring the security and correctness of code produced by generative AI.

stories.title: Are You Using Coding Agents Like Slot Machines?
stories.author: loicboset
bullet_points: Coding agents are significantly accelerating software development timelines.
The rapid adoption of AI tools is a major trend across industries.
The article raises a cautionary point about the potentially uncritical use of these AI tools.
